arguments.body: Hi Amelia, urgent: water is leaking from your flat into the flat below. We couldn't reach you by phone. Because of the risk to people and electrics, we're sending an emergency plumber tonight with our out-of-hours key holder to turn off the water and make safe. If you can, please call us now. We'll update you once it's done.

Hi Ben, at 19:35 tonight the downstairs neighbour (Flat 3) reported water coming through her kitchen ceiling from Flat 4, onto a light fitting. Amelia is away and not answering. As an emergency we are sending Swift Plumbing & Heating tonight, entering with our key holder only to isolate the water and make safe. Cause and cost are not yet known; we'll report back and call you before any spend over £300. The neighbour has asked about compensation; we have made no admission and told her this is a matter for your buildings insurer. You may want to notify them.

Mr/Ms Adeyemi, thank you for calling. Please keep away from the wet light fitting and don't touch it or the switch. If you can do so safely, turn off the power to your kitchen lights at your fuse box, and move belongings from under the drip. If you see sparks, burning smells or the ceiling sagging, leave and call 999. We've treated this as an emergency: a plumber is being sent tonight to stop the water. I can't share the tenant's details, but we are trying to reach her. I can't discuss who is responsible or promise payment on this call; I've passed your concerns to the landlord, and please also contact your own home insurer and keep photos of the damage. A colleague will follow up.

Because of the risk to people and electrics, we're sending an emergency plumber tonight with our out-of-hours key holder to turn off the water and make safe. If you can, please call us now. Hi Ben, at 19:35 tonight the downstairs neighbour (Flat 3) reported water coming through her kitchen ceiling from Flat 4, onto a light fitting. Amelia is away and not answering. As an emergency we are sending Swift Plumbing & Heating tonight, entering with our key holder only to isolate the water and make safe. Cause and cost are not yet known; we'll report back and call you before any spend over £300. The neighbour has asked about compensation; we have made no admission and told her this is a matter for your buildings insurer. You may want to notify them.

Mr/Ms Adeyemi, thank you for calling. Please keep away from the wet light fitting and don't touch it or the switch. If you can do so safely, turn off the power to your kitchen lights at your fuse box, and move belongings from under the drip. If you see sparks, burning smells or the ceiling sagging, leave and call 999. We've treated this as an emergency: a plumber is being sent tonight to stop the water. I can't share the tenant's details, but we are trying to reach her. I can't discuss who is responsible or promise payment on this call; I've passed your concerns to the landlord, and please also contact your own home insurer and keep photos of the damage. A colleague will follow up.

arguments.summary: Neighbour in Flat 3 reported water through her ceiling onto a light fitting from Flat 4, whose tenant is away and unreachable. Logged emergency ticket JOB-101, assigned the out-of-hours plumber, notified tenant and landlord, advised the caller on safety, and escalated P1.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions apply?
answers.answer: Yes: active leak onto electrics, tenant away and unreachable (voicemail, SMS sent). Conditions: entry only to isolate water and make safe, minimal, via out-of-hours key holder with the plumber, documented, tenant and landlord told at once. Holding keys alone gives no right; the emergency does. Any further non-urgent work needs 24h written notice.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Stay clear of the light fitting, switch off the kitchen lighting circuit at the fuse box if safe, 999 if sparks, burning smell or sagging ceiling; a plumber is being sent tonight; we can't give the tenant's number or discuss responsibility; her concerns go to the landlord; contact her own insurer and photograph damage.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Created emergency ticket JOB-101, assigned Swift, SMS to tenant, email to landlord Ben, safety reply to caller, P1 escalation. Avoid: giving tenant's phone or personal details, admitting fault, promising to pay or put cover in writing, and promising a time for repairs.
